articles.title: The color of your hair may change how even your skin looks to others
articles.summary: Darker hair and black backgrounds can make facial skin appear more even, according to new research in Perception. The skin itself was never altered, suggesting contrast around the face shapes how others perceive it.

articles.title: A father’s scent helps babies synchronize their brains with new adults
articles.summary: The scent of a father can help infants synchronize their brain activity with unfamiliar adults. A recent study reveals that paternal body odor boosts positive arousal and neural coupling, helping babies expand their social connections.

articles.summary: A recent investigation suggests that the presence or removal of Confederate monuments does not alter people's racial biases.

articles.title: Cannabis users were twice as likely to commit violence, review finds
articles.summary: A review of more than 265,000 people found that cannabis use was associated with higher rates of both committing violence and becoming a victim of it. The researchers say the link is significant but does not prove cannabis itself is the cause.

articles.title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
articles.summary: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat. Researchers say the results strengthen the case for creatine as a potentially useful tool for maintaining muscle with age.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging. The strongest effects appeared in Alzheimer’s and mild cognitive impairment, while ADHD and autism showed no significant overall difference.

articles.title: Children at risk for depression get “stuck” on sad faces
articles.summary: Depression may change which emotional faces children notice most, but the pattern appears to depend on family history. Children at higher familial risk became increasingly focused on sad faces, while lower-risk children with rising symptoms paid less attention to happy ones.

articles.title: Weight-loss drug semaglutide alters reward-seeking behavior in healthy mice
articles.summary: A new study in healthy mice reveals that the popular weight-loss drug semaglutide alters behavior and brain activity related to reward and stress, shifting how animals pursue natural rewards and react to stressful situations.

articles.title: A single dose of MDMA prevents trauma-fueled drinking in genetically prone rats
articles.summary: A study in rats suggests MDMA can prevent the rise in alcohol intake that follows trauma-like stress, but only in animals genetically predisposed to drink heavily. The effect did not appear to depend on changes in fear.

articles.title: Psychologists identify the musical triggers of beauty and the sublime
articles.summary: A new psychology study reveals that minor musical keys evoke the sublime, major keys predict beauty, and visual elements heavily dominate our overall aesthetic responses when we experience audio and visual media simultaneously.

articles.title: Childhood war exposure might shift the neural correlates of attachment-related anxiety and avoidance
articles.summary: When war broke out in October 2023, an Israeli brain-imaging study was already underway. Comparing children scanned before and during the war, researchers found that attachment-related characteristics were tied to different patterns of emotional brain connectivity.

articles.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
articles.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.

articles.title: Neurosymbolic Routing for Reliable Reasoning on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.35833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Running a language model on edge hardware provides private and low-latency reasoning without a network connection, and yet the small models that fit on such devices are unreliable on the tasks computers are expected to handle well, such as arithmetic, algebra, and formal logic problems. We argue that much of this unreliability is avoidable. Many queries appearing to demand reasoning are in fact structurally deterministic and permit fast and exact symbolic solutions. Therefore, forcing a probabilistic model to approximate them sacrifices accuracy
